name: release_structure_if_active
description: Returns -1 when the pointer is null or its active field is zero. Otherwise it optionally calls two other routines to release attached resources, clears the active field, calls one more routine, and returns 0 only if every step succeeded.

name: open_stream_from_mode_string
description: Parses a two-character access mode made of read, write, append and optional plus signs into flag bits, then calls another routine to open the file. On success it fills in the structure's fields and returns it; an unrecognised mode returns a null pointer.

name: find_or_allocate_free_node
description: Walks a linked list hanging off a global structure looking for a node whose count field is zero. If none is free, it allocates and zeroes a new node, links it into the list, and passes the node to a other routine.

name: format_one_conversion_specifier
description: Handles one printf-style conversion: it reads flags, width, precision and length modifiers, converts an integer, character, string or pointer argument into text, and pads it. It returns the position after the specifier, or a null pointer for an unsupported conversion.

name: emit_format_string_characters
description: Walks a printf-style format string and passes each literal character to an output routine, treating a doubled percent sign as one literal. Other conversion specifiers are skipped through another routine, and the walk stops at the end of the string.

name: delete_file_save_error_code
description: Calls the DOS library to delete a file. When that call returns zero, it saves the DOS error code and a second result, and the routine returns true in that case.

name: do_nothing_stub
description: Does nothing: the routine is a bare return with no operations. It is a stub with no behaviour to describe.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one other routine and returns, with no other work on data, registers or memory.

name: program_entry_setup_sequence
description: Program entry point. It calls other routines and a library function through a stored pointer, runs a short loop of other-routine calls, then clears a saved word and, when a structure field matches an expected pattern, saves that field and writes a fixed marker value.

name: decrement_until_minus_one
description: Decrements a 16-bit variable repeatedly until it wraps to negative one, then returns. The loop has no other work, so it acts as a short countdown delay.

name: setup_hardware_and_run_loop
description: Program entry point for the start-up code. It opens a system library through a stored base, copies values from its structure, and writes the DMA control and interrupt registers, then runs a long frame loop that polls input bits and updates counters until a flag ends it.

name: save_chip_state_mask_interrupts
description: Saves several custom-chip register values into a structure, clears all interrupt enables and requests, and stores two interrupt-handler pointers. It then enables a selected set of interrupt bits.

name: restore_chip_state_from_structure
description: Clears the interrupt request bits, then writes back saved values for several custom-chip registers from a structure, including the interrupt enables and the DMA control. Finally it sets the DMA bits from the saved state.

name: copy_state_then_call_libraries
description: Copies two saved values into a structure and calls a chain of library functions through a stored library base, recording the first result. It clears two flag bytes and sets a counter, then, if a further flag is set, calls a stored routine and closes a library.

name: drive_cia_port_pattern
description: Writes all ones to a CIA port register, then a fixed byte pattern with another routine call between writes, and finally all ones again. The routine calls separate the writes.

name: load_resources_run_frame_loop
description: Opens the DOS and graphics libraries through their stored bases, allocates working memory, and sets up display and interrupt registers. It then runs a frame loop that polls the fire-button inputs, updates counters and calls other routines, with a progress percentage shown during loading.

name: forward_to_routine
description: The decompiled body is only a single call to another routine followed by a return, so the rest of the work cannot be seen in this code.

name: call_five_routines
description: Calls five other routines in sequence and then returns, with no other work in this body.

name: advance_timed_sequence_step
description: Returns early when a flag byte is set. Otherwise it increments a stored counter and, at certain counter values, sets a display value and calls another routine; at one later value it calls a routine through a stored pointer and sets a completion flag.

name: find_matching_table_entry
description: Scans a table of fixed-size records and counts those whose flag byte is clear and whose position falls in a small window around a target. It stores the index of a qualifying record, falling back to a second index when no record carries the special flag.

name: find_matching_record_by_tag
description: Scans a table of fixed-size records, matching each record's tag byte against a value and checking that its position falls within a window around a target. It stores a chosen index, preferring a flagged record and falling back to another.

name: update_button_state_flags
description: Stores a fixed value in a structure, then derives two flags from individual bits of a stored state byte. It also calls other routines that read the fire-button input and store their results.

name: advance_state_machine_map_check
description: Advances a small state machine by one step. Depending on the current state it decrements a stored counter and marks an action, and in one state it checks tile codes in a grid table, where codes of one, two, three or ten block movement.

name: step_position_toward_target
description: Moves a 16-bit position one step toward a target value. The step is four normally, or sixteen when a flag is set and the result stays below the target, and nothing changes once the target is reached.

name: step_position_down_to_zero
description: Reduces a stored 16-bit position toward zero, by four normally or by sixteen when a flag is set and the result stays non-negative. Nothing changes when the position is already zero.

name: do_nothing_stub
description: The decompiled body is only a return, with no operations visible. It is a stub, or its real body did not decompile.

name: set_state_word_call_routine
description: Stores a fixed default value in one field of a structure and then calls a other routine.

name: calculate_record_offset
description: Takes a 16-bit index, subtracts one from it and returns the result multiplied by the size of a 44-byte record.

name: pack_position_into_word_pair
description: Packs a row and a column into two 16-bit words after adding fixed offsets and shifting the column, and returns the pair. The second word gets a fixed offset plus the low bit of the column.

name: pack_position_into_word_pair
description: Packs a row and a column into two 16-bit words after adding fixed offsets and shifting the column, and returns the pair. This variant uses a different fixed offset for the second word.

name: pack_position_into_word_pair
description: Packs a row and a column into two 16-bit words after adding fixed offsets and shifting the column, and returns the pair. This variant adds a larger fixed offset to the second word.

name: do_nothing_stub
description: The routine is a bare return with no operations visible in the decompiled code. It is a stub, or its real body did not decompile.

name: store_routine_result_with_offset
description: Calls another routine and stores its result in one global variable, then stores a second global variable set to that result plus a fixed offset.

name: advance_two_phase_countdown
description: Runs a two-phase countdown on a structure: while one flag is clear it counts a timer down, and at zero it toggles the phase and reloads the timer. Otherwise it clears the phase flag and returns a stored status value.

name: handle_keypress_command
description: Dispatches on a key code: one key resets stored fields, another restores saved values and starts a countdown, and another toggles a flag. Digit keys select an index value, and two keys step that index up or down within a range of eight.

name: set_width_from_mode_flag
description: Marks a flag byte as set, then assigns a width-like field either from a stored value or from a fixed default, depending on a mode flag.

name: set_default_dimension_fields
description: Writes a fixed default value into two dimension fields of a structure.

name: draw_glyph_string_to_bitplanes
description: Walks a byte-coded string and copies each character's glyph rows from a font table into four bitplanes of the target bitmap. A special code moves the position back one column, and a transparency flag makes the glyph combine with existing pixels instead of overwriting them.

name: acknowledge_cia_interrupt_bits
description: Reads a CIA interrupt-control byte, calls another routine when one bit is set and another when a second bit is set, then acknowledges the matching interrupt request in the interrupt request register.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Reads one byte from the keyboard serial register, rearranges its bits into a key code and performs a handshake on the control register. It then updates key-state flags for certain codes, or looks up a character in a key table and stores it.

name: split_number_by_ten_thousand
description: Divides a 32-bit number by ten thousand, packs the quotient and remainder into a pair of 16-bit words, and passes that pair to another routine. It then calls a second routine.

name: format_high_word_four_digits
description: Converts the upper 16-bit half of a value into four decimal digit characters and packs them into one 32-bit result, most significant digit first.

name: set_bitplane_pointers_for_frame
description: Toggles a frame flag and picks one of two buffer addresses from it, storing that address in a structure. It then writes four bitplane pointer pairs into a table, each stepping by a fixed stride.

name: wait_for_fire_button_press
description: Polls the input register in a loop, calling another routine when one particular key code arrives, and keeps looping until the fire-button bit pattern changes. It then returns the pressed bits.

name: decrement_countdown_timer_with_borrow
description: Advances a frame counter and, when the gating conditions allow, decrements a two-level countdown. The low field reloads from a stored value and borrows from the high field when it goes negative.

name: wait_until_flag_set
description: Clears a flag byte and then busy-waits until another code path sets it to a nonzero value.

name: poll_until_routine_returns_zero
description: Calls another routine in a loop and keeps repeating until the routine returns zero, which acts as a polling wait.

name: fill_three_rows_of_entries
description: When a counter field is nonzero, it decrements the counter and fills three runs of entries, of 32, 8 and 16 items, by calling another routine for each item and storing the result in a structure.

name: fill_grid_cells_from_routine
description: Runs nested loops over a block of cells, calling other routines to compute a value for each cell and storing it at a fixed offset in a structure.

name: fill_rows_from_routine_values
description: An outer loop of sixteen iterations calls two other routines, then an inner loop of thirty-two iterations stores another routine-supplied value at a fixed offset.

name: step_packed_position_toward_target
description: Compares a current packed position with a target one nibble at a time and moves the position one unit closer in each field. The high nibble is checked last, and the routine returns early when the current value is already below it.

name: reset_two_pointer_fields
description: Calls another routine, then points two pointer fields in its structures at a fixed global address.

name: reset_two_pointer_fields
description: Calls another routine, then points two pointer fields in its structures at a fixed global address.

name: reset_two_pointer_fields
description: Calls another routine, then points two pointer fields in its structures at a fixed global address.

name: initialise_table_entries
description: Writes a set of fixed address and size words into a table of entries. If a mode flag is set it also stores results from another routine into two pointer fields; otherwise it clears several fields and writes a smaller set of entries.

name: set_pointer_table_for_planes
description: Fills a table of pointer pairs: three entries step by a large stride, then four entries step by a smaller stride. It also writes four fixed words into register pairs and returns the final pointer.

name: set_fixed_pointer_pairs
description: Writes four fixed 32-bit values, each split into a pair of 16-bit words, into four register pairs. The input value is passed through unchanged.

name: set_fixed_pointer_pairs
description: Writes four fixed 32-bit values, each split into a pair of 16-bit words, into four register pairs. The input value is passed through unchanged.

name: fill_pointer_table_with_stride
description: Loops four times, writing successive pointers that step by a fixed stride into a table of eight-byte entries.

name: copy_bitmap_planes_and_clear
description: Copies planar bitmap data from a source block into interleaved bitplane memory, writing each source word into several destination rows. It then clears a block of 4160 longwords to zero.

name: copy_bitmap_block_into_planes
description: Copies a source bitmap block into interleaved bitplane memory, writing each source word into several destination rows at fixed row offsets.

name: clear_bitplane_memory_block
description: Zeroes a large block of memory by writing zero longwords in pairs for a fixed number of iterations.

name: call_routine_when_flagged
description: Calls a other routine, then calls a second routine before returning only when a flag byte in the structure is set.

name: store_computed_table_entries
description: Copies two 16-bit fields into a backup pair, then calls other routines to compute values and stores each result in several table entries. It finally selects one of two global addresses by a flag and stores its low and high words.

name: store_computed_table_entry
description: Copies two 16-bit fields into a backup pair, calls another routine to compute a value and stores it in a table entry. It then selects one of two global addresses by a flag and stores its low and high words.

name: update_position_with_clamping
description: Updates a two-dimensional position by the difference between its stored and new coordinates. Horizontal values are clamped to a bound that depends on a mode flag, and vertical values are clamped to a fixed maximum.

name: check_completion_condition
description: Returns the value of another routine, and when a flag is set it runs a sequence of routine steps and sums two counters. If that sum is zero and the conditions match, it sets a done flag and returns zero.

name: compute_percent_and_store_output
description: Computes a percentage as one value times one hundred divided by a total and stores it. It then writes values from routine calls into two output buffers and sets a completion flag when a counter reaches a target.

name: write_status_label_for_state
description: Fills a 12-byte output buffer with a text label chosen from a status value. When no status is set it writes a row of colons, otherwise it writes a fixed label for each recognised status code.

name: format_colon_separated_digits
description: Writes colon separators into a text buffer and fills in the decimal digits of a value, dropping leading zero digits.

name: format_two_digit_colon_field
description: Writes two colons into a text buffer, then a one- or two-digit number with any leading zero left out.

name: format_word_as_four_digits
description: Converts a 16-bit value into four decimal digit characters and packs them into one 32-bit result, most significant digit first.

name: draw_two_digit_number
description: For a nonzero value, looks up font rows for the tens and ones digits and copies them into bitplane positions. For zero it clears mask bits at eight row positions instead.

name: advance_active_entry_counters
description: Returns early when a flag byte is set. Otherwise it steps through thirty-two entries, advancing a counter for each active one and computing a position from it and a multiplier.

name: process_all_active_entries
description: When a flag is set it first resets a counter field and calls other routines. It then loops over thirty-two entries, calling another routine for each active one and returning the last value.

name: process_active_entries_loop
description: Loops over thirty-two entries and calls another routine for each active one, returning the value from the last active entry processed.

name: clear_word_table
description: Zeroes a large table of 16-bit words by writing zero to a fixed number of consecutive words.

name: fill_rectangles_into_bitmap
description: For each of sixteen entries with a nonzero size, fills a rectangle in the bitmap with a value combining the entry index and a stored pattern. Rows advance by a fixed stride.

name: fill_marked_rectangles_with_value
description: For each non-empty entry in a table of thirty-two, fills its rectangle in the bitmap with a fixed value of nine, stepping rows by a fixed stride.

name: spawn_next_queued_entry
description: Counts a timer down and, when it reaches zero, reloads it and fills the next slot of a table of records from a cycling source list, then advances the slot count. A flag can cycle two counters first.

name: refresh_level_info_display
description: Redraws level information when the selected level changes. It looks up a value in a table, writes a formatted number, sets a one-character level digit, and copies sixteen words of table data into a display buffer.

name: load_colour_palette_from_record
description: Searches a data block for a four-character colour map tag, then unpacks seven packed nibble groups into 16-bit palette words and writes them to a buffer.

name: copy_table_block_by_index
description: Copies 512 longwords from one of four blocks of a table, chosen by an index value, into a buffer.

name: set_handler_pointer_for_index
description: Stores a pointer in a structure, computed as a base routine address plus a stored index multiplied by a fixed stride.

name: initialise_entry_state_fields
description: Resets a block of state fields in a structure from stored source values and derives several fields from a computed value. When a mode flag is set it also computes a further pair of positions, clamped to a limit.

name: copy_input_record_into_state
description: Copies nine values from an input record into fixed fields of a structure, then clears four counter fields and a flag byte.

name: run_entry_updates_active_slots
description: Calls two other routines, then either walks a sentinel-terminated list calling another routine for each item or calls one routine. It finally calls another routine for each of thirty-two active entries and returns the last result.

name: run_sentinel_list_updates
description: Calls two other routines, then either walks a sentinel-terminated list calling another routine for each item or calls one routine. It then calls four more other routines.

name: copy_active_entry_rows
description: For each of thirty-two entries that is active, copies a 33-byte row from a source table into a buffer at that entry's row position.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one other routine and returns, with no other work visible in the code.

name: run_blit_sequence_with_waits
description: Sets up a blit-related structure, then writes a fixed size word and waits for the blitter busy bit to clear. It repeats this write-and-wait sequence four times.

name: build_row_offset_table
description: Fills a table of 184 words with successive multiples of 204, giving row offsets, then clears a further run of 48 words.

name: update_saved_percentage_display
description: Computes a saved percentage from two counters and copies its digits into a status message. It also chooses a plural ending from the first digit of the level number.

name: copy_large_word_block
description: Copies a large block of 16-bit words from a source pointer into a buffer, counting a 16-bit counter down until it wraps around.

name: call_two_routines
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns.

name: call_two_routines
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns.

name: build_active_entry_positions
description: Scans thirty-two entries and, for each one whose flag is one, stores a packed position from its coordinates plus an offset. It then fills one to four slots with that position, a default, or a copy of earlier slots, depending on how many matched.

name: copy_first_flagged_entry_position
description: Scans thirty-two entries and, at the first one whose flag equals two, copies its two packed position fields into a structure and stops.

name: pack_state_bits_rotate_buffer
description: Packs flag bits from several state bytes into a set of bitplane bytes, then sums eight bytes into a nibble. It rotates eight bytes through a shifting buffer, calls two routines and clears a flag.

name: wait_for_register_change
description: Repeats a spin that waits for the high byte of a word in a structure to change, using the input value as the repeat count.

name: update_fire_button_latch
description: Reads a stored input byte. When the fire-button bit is clear it resets the state byte to zero, and when the state byte is zero it sets it to all ones.

name: advance_text_entry_character
description: Counts a timer down and, when it reaches zero, reloads it and writes the next character from a source table into an entry buffer. It toggles an underscore cursor character as it goes.

name: load_file_into_buffer
description: Locks, opens and reads a file through the DOS library into a buffer, then stores the loaded address in the copper pointer fields. On failure it shows an error message, releases memory and closes the library.

name: copy_byte_block
description: Copies a count of bytes from a source address to a destination address, one byte at a time.

name: enter_name_from_keyboard
description: Reads keyboard codes into a short name buffer, handling backspace, delete and cursor-movement codes and uppercasing letters. It then checks a nibble checksum over the buffer and, when it matches, rotates a bit buffer and stores a status flag with its label.

name: reset_state_fields_and_routines
description: Clears several state fields of a structure, conditionally calls another routine, clears a further field when a flag is zero, and then calls three other routines.

name: setup_fixed_dimensions_and_routines
description: Calls two other routines, sets two dimension fields and a buffer pointer to fixed values, clears a flag, and then calls a sequence of sixteen other routines.

name: select_panel_one
description: Writes the character for one into a panel selection byte, clears a flag in the structure, and calls two other routines.

name: select_panel_two
description: Writes the character for two into a panel selection byte, sets a flag in the structure, and calls two other routines.

name: cycle_animated_entries
description: Walks seven entries, decrementing each one's delay counter. When a delay expires it advances a four-state frame index, reloads the delay, and calls another routine.

name: advance_frame_and_decrement_counters
description: Advances a four-bit frame counter and reloads a delay, then calls another routine. It walks a list of counters, decrementing each one until a sentinel count is reached.

name: handle_name_entry_input
description: Reads keyboard codes into a name buffer, handling backspace, delete and cursor-movement codes and uppercasing letters. It then checks a nibble checksum over the buffer and, when it matches, rotates a bit buffer and stores a status label.

name: initialise_panel_dimensions
description: Sets fixed dimension fields in a structure, points a buffer field at a global address, clears an offset field, and calls another routine whose result is stored in a pointer field.

name: forward_to_routine
description: Calls one other routine and returns its value unchanged.

name: copy_interleaved_table_rows
description: Copies a word table into an interleaved buffer across eighty groups, writing fourteen words per group at a fixed stride.

name: handle_name_entry_input
description: Reads keyboard codes into a name buffer, handling backspace, delete and cursor-movement codes and uppercasing letters. It then checks a nibble checksum over the buffer and, when it matches, rotates a bit buffer and stores a status label.

name: draw_glyph_string_to_bitplanes
description: Walks a byte-coded string and copies each character's glyph rows from a font table into four bitplanes of the target bitmap. A special code moves the position back one column, and a transparency flag makes the glyph combine with existing pixels instead of overwriting them.

name: draw_glyph_string_to_bitplanes
description: Walks a byte-coded string and copies each character's glyph rows from a font table into four bitplanes of the target bitmap. A special code moves the position back one column, and a transparency flag makes the glyph combine with existing pixels instead of overwriting them.

name: update_entry_mask_bits
description: Clears a block of mask memory, then for each active entry moves a bit from one mask plane to another at a position derived from the entry's coordinates.

name: build_row_pointer_table
description: Returns early when a flag is set. Otherwise it computes a base address from a position and writes a table of sixteen row pointers, each advanced by the width of the previous row, with routine calls supplying the offsets.

name: call_routine_then_stored_handler
description: Calls one routine and then calls a routine through a stored pointer before returning.

name: toggle_state_byte_and_call
description: When a flag is set, toggles one of two state bytes depending on whether a stored position lies past a threshold. It then calls a routine through a stored pointer.

name: decompress_bitstream_into_buffer
description: Decodes a packed bit stream, read backwards, into a buffer. Each control bit selects either a literal copy or a copy of earlier output at a computed distance, and the routine stops when the output pointer reaches the start.

name: shift_bit_reader_by_count
description: Shifts a 32-bit bit buffer right by a count, pulling in a new word from memory whenever the buffer empties.

name: unpack_packbits_body_chunk
description: Searches for a body data chunk and decodes its run-length packed rows into a bitmap. It advances to the next row after each row's width and stops when the row count reaches zero.

name: combine_three_planes_with_or
description: ORs three source bitplanes word by word into a destination buffer over a fixed count.

name: unpack_packbits_body_chunk
description: Searches for a body data chunk and decodes its run-length packed rows into a bitmap, using a different row width and row count from the other unpacking variant.

name: unpack_packbits_body_chunk
description: Searches for a body data chunk and decodes its run-length packed rows into a bitmap, advancing rows by a stored stride.

name: wait_raster_line_then_reset
description: Polls the vertical beam position up to a fixed number of times, waiting for it to pass a threshold. If it never does it sets a flag, then sets a counter and a position field, adding a step when that flag is set.

name: run_shutdown_sequence
description: Calls a long sequence of other routines, then calls two routines through stored pointers and finishes with more other routines. The referenced text names an end picture and an end sample.

name: decompress_level_data_stream
description: Decodes a packed bit stream of level data, read backwards, into a buffer. Control bits choose between literal copies and back-references to earlier output, and on completion it checks a running checksum before continuing with its display setup.

name: move_entry_across_bit_map
description: Moves an entry across a bitplane map one step at a time. It tests a column of map bits near its position to decide how far it can go, then updates its position, timers and state flags.

name: do_nothing_stub
description: The decompiled body is a bare return, so no behaviour is visible. The real routine did not decompile into readable code.

name: advance_entry_when_timer_expires
description: Decrements a stored delay counter and, once it reaches zero, sets up the entry's state fields and steps through a list of entries, calling other routines as needed.

name: initialise_entry_motion_state
description: Writes a masked flag word with a fixed bit set, sets two offset fields to fixed values, and clears two counters in an entry structure.

name: clear_mask_bits_four_planes
description: ANDs a mask word into four words of bitplane memory at fixed row offsets, clearing the masked bits in each.

name: copy_entry_pixel_bytes_rows
description: Computes a bitmap offset from a position, copies three bytes of an entry's pixel data into three rows spaced at fixed strides, and stores a flag word.

name: apply_map_code_to_entry
description: Reads a map code at the entry's position and applies its effect. Some codes flip the horizontal direction, some set a marker in a status table, and others set up a new state with fixed offsets.

name: initialise_entry_position_limits
description: Sets position offset fields and fixed initial values for an entry, selects a horizontal limit depending on a mode flag, and calls other routines to finish the setup.

name: draw_active_entries_with_blitter
description: Loops over the active entries that fall within the visible range, computes each one's screen position and frame from its state flags, and writes each sprite to the bitmap through blitter passes, waiting for the blitter between passes.

name: update_bit_planes_scan_entries
description: Sets or clears one bit at a position across four bitplanes, then walks a list of entries. It calls other routines for those within the horizontal range, using a lookup table to choose the drawing routine for each.

name: update_bit_planes_scan_entries
description: Sets or clears one bit at a position across four bitplanes, then walks a list of entries. It calls other routines for those within the horizontal range, using a lookup table to choose the drawing routine for each.

name: update_bit_planes_scan_entries
description: Sets or clears one bit at a position across four bitplanes, then walks a list of entries. It calls other routines for those within the horizontal range, using a lookup table to choose the drawing routine for each.

name: update_bit_planes_scan_entries
description: Sets or clears one bit at a position across four bitplanes, then walks a list of entries. It calls other routines for those within the horizontal range, using a lookup table to choose the drawing routine for each.

name: update_bit_planes_scan_entries
description: Sets or clears one bit at a position across four bitplanes, then walks a list of entries. It calls other routines for those within the horizontal range, using a lookup table to choose the drawing routine for each.

name: queue_blit_for_entry_tile
description: Looks up a tile from an entry's position, computes an address in the bitmap, and writes four groups of row pointers into the blitter setup. It waits for the blitter to finish between groups.

name: queue_bitplane_blit_rows
description: Rounds a stored offset to a 16-bit boundary to derive a shift, then writes four groups of row pointers into the blitter setup. It waits for the blitter to finish between groups.

name: queue_bitplane_blit_rows
description: Rounds a stored offset to a 16-bit boundary to derive a shift, then writes four groups of row pointers into the blitter setup. It waits for the blitter to finish between groups.

name: draw_character_glyphs_to_screen
description: Walks a string until a negative byte, copying the glyph for each non-space character from a font table into a screen buffer. Each glyph is a fixed block of words laid out across rows.

name: apply_routine_to_24_rows
description: When a mode flag is clear, loops over twenty-four rows and calls another routine on each row's data and destination pointer.

name: pack_column_mask_bits
description: Advances a row index stored in a structure, then for twenty rows packs eight source bytes into one byte. Each bit is set when its source byte has any of bits two to four set.

name: pack_column_mask_bits
description: For twenty rows, packs eight source bytes into one byte. Each bit is set when its source byte has any of bits two to four set.

name: clear_four_plane_word_columns
description: Walks a run of 408 positions, zeroing a word in each of four bitplane arrays at fixed strides, which clears those columns in every plane.

name: convert_bitplane_words_to_pixels
description: Expands each 32-bit bitplane word into byte values by weighting selected bit positions, then writes four results into destination rows at fixed offsets. Repeats for fifty rows of forty columns.

name: start_blit_four_times_waiting
description: Sets the blitter fields and writes a fixed blit size word four times, waiting for the blitter to finish after each write.

name: paint_edge_masks_for_column
description: Computes a column offset from a stored value and ORs an edge mask into two bitplane words. The mask and target planes are chosen by whether the value passes a threshold and by a flag.

name: clear_plane_edge_bits_rows
description: Loops over 160 rows, clearing and setting edge bits in the first and last words of four bitplanes.

name: advance_scroll_and_blit_rows
description: Advances a scroll offset by four units and, until it reaches its limit, copies row data through the blitter. When the offset wraps, it counts a timer down, writes a marker character and calls other routines.

name: advance_frame_index_call_routines
description: Increments a stored index with wraparound at thirty-two, then calls two other routines.

name: store_bitmap_row_geometry
description: Stores a pixel width, that width divided by eight as bytes per row, a height value, and the product of bytes per row and height into global variables.

name: store_two_global_words
description: Stores its two 16-bit inputs into a pair of global variables.

name: blit_tile_rows_with_masks
description: Draws a rectangle of tiles into the bitmap through the blitter. It computes a start address and per-row offsets from the tile geometry, then loops over rows, choosing a blit control word from mode flags and waiting for the blitter on each row.

name: clip_rectangle_to_bounds
description: Clips a rectangle against limits stored in a structure. When a flag is set it computes a horizontal shift in steps of sixteen, and it returns all ones when the vertical position falls outside the bounds.

name: call_six_routines
description: Calls six other routines in sequence and returns, with no other work visible in the code.

name: store_half_sizes_and_pointers
description: Looks up a table entry by index after calling another routine, stores half of two size fields from an input record into it, and stores two pointers to that record's data at fixed positions.

name: setup_audio_channels_from_mask
description: For each of four bits in the input mask, clears that audio channel's DMA bit, points the channel at a sample address with a length of one, and records the channel in a state byte.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: call_routines_when_flag_clear
description: Calls three other routines, then calls four more only when a stored flag is zero.

name: disable_audio_dma_channels
description: Calls another routine, sets a stored flag to one, then clears the DMA enable bits for the first four audio channels.

name: loop_forever_setting_field
description: Repeats forever, writing a fixed value to one field of a structure, so the routine never returns.

name: check_checksum_and_patch_code
description: Compares the sum of four stored words against a fixed check value and, when they differ, overwrites a code word with a no-operation instruction.

name: start_cia_timer_with_interrupt
description: For one of two input codes, sets two pointer fields and programs a CIA timer: it writes the interrupt control bits and starts the timer at its maximum count.

name: reset_channel_state_block
description: Stores an input value, clears a block of state bytes in a structure, then sets four counter fields to a fixed value of sixty-three.

name: call_three_routines

name: store_half_sizes_and_pointers
description: Looks up a table entry by index after calling another routine, stores half of two size fields from an input record into it, and stores two pointers to that record's data at fixed positions.

name: find_four_byte_sequence
description: Scans forward through memory until it finds a four-byte sequence equal to the input value, and returns when the end address is reached.

name: do_nothing_stub
description: The routine is a bare return with no operations visible in the decompiled code. It is a stub.

name: walk_linked_list_calling_routine
description: Walks a zero-terminated linked list, calling another routine on each node and following its link until a zero link is reached.

name: return_argument_unchanged
description: Returns the value passed on the stack without any other operation.

name: store_three_bytes_and_pointers
description: Uses an index to look up a table slot, stores three bytes from an input pointer into it, and writes a pointer located nine bytes before that input into four fixed-offset fields.

name: walk_linked_list_calling_routine

name: call_two_routines
description: Calls two other routines in sequence and returns.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns its input value unchanged.

name: reset_entry_slot_fields
description: Copies a stored word into the first field of a structure, sets one byte to all ones, and clears two more bytes.

name: copy_slot_bytes_to_outputs
description: Looks up a slot by index and calls four other routines. Unless the slot's first byte is all ones, it copies two of the slot's bytes into two output locations.

name: rotate_byte_right_by_one
description: When bit zero of the input is set, it stores a pointer, clears a word and a byte in a structure. It then returns the input byte rotated right by one bit.

name: call_five_routines
description: Calls five other routines in sequence and returns, with no other work in this body.

name: store_packed_bytes_into_entry
description: When bit zero of the flags is set, copies three bytes of a 32-bit input into fields of a structure, copying the top byte only when a sub-flag is clear, and clears one more byte.

name: setup_audio_channels_from_mask
description: For each of four bits in the input mask, clears that audio channel's DMA bit, points the channel at a sample address with a length of one, and records the channel in a state byte.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: initialise_entry_byte_fields
description: When bit zero of the flags is set, writes one to one byte of a structure, copies the input byte into two adjacent bytes, and sets a fourth byte to all ones.

name: call_routines_when_flag_clear
description: Calls three other routines, then calls four more only when a stored flag is zero.

name: decrement_counter_or_reload_five
description: When the stored counter is zero it reloads it to five. Otherwise it decrements the counter by one.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: copy_three_table_bytes
description: When a flag in a referenced structure is clear, copies three consecutive bytes from a table, starting at an index, into three fields of the current structure.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: advance_frame_when_delay_expires
description: Decrements a delay counter in a referenced structure, and once it expires advances a word at the start of that structure by twelve.

name: call_four_routines
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: copy_entry_record_and_rotate
description: When a stored word is nonzero, copies a record of several fields to another location, writes the input word into a register field, clears the source word and sets a flag byte in another structure. It returns the input byte rotated left by one bit.
